conversations.answer: Your code appears to be mostly correct, however, there's one key point you need to consider when using ES6 modules in the browser. The exported members are not directly available in the global scope. Therefore, the initGame function isn't accessible within the global scope during window.onload, even though you have exported the Game class from the module.To solve this, you can move the initGame function inside the Game class and export an instance of the Game class instead.Below are the changes to consider:game.js[CODE_BLOCK_0]Your HTML would then remain the same.About the console error "Error with Permissions-Policy header: Origin trial controlled feature not enabled: 'interest-cohort'", it's related to the Google's FLoC (Federated Learning of Cohorts) trial. This message doesn't relate to your problem and should not interfere with your application.Note: I would advise using const and let over var for variable declaration. const and let have block scope and can prevent a lot of bugs related to variable hoisting and accidental reassignments.

conversations.answer: My apologies for misunderstanding. You're right. The error is at import Game from './game.js'; in your test file. The problem arises because of the window.game = new Game(); line in your game.js.The Jest environment, which is based on Node.js, does not have a global window object like you would in a browser environment, so when game.js tries to access window, it returns undefined, and trying to set a property on undefined throws a TypeError.To avoid this issue, you should check if the window object exists before setting a property on it. Change your game.js to look like this:[CODE_BLOCK_0]If you have already added this condition and you still face issues, then it's likely the problem is due to the fact that Jest is running in a Node.js environment and is unable to access the DOM API in the same way that a browser can. To solve this issue, you can use jsdom as a test environment to simulate a browser-like environment in Node.js.In your Jest configuration (which may be in your package.json or in a jest.config.js file), set the testEnvironment property to "jsdom". Your configuration might look something like this:[CODE_BLOCK_1]Then, Jest will be able to understand your DOM manipulations and should be able to run your tests as expected. If you're already using jsdom and still encountering issues, then please let me know so I can help you further.
